walkForward.survivorshipEligibility: an observation on a KR security enters training or evaluation only if pipeline.alpha_opportunity_v4_eligibility.label_eligibility(completeness=..., window_crosses_termination=...) reports ELIGIBLE for that (security, signal date, horizon). `completeness` is the sealed completeness row for the security if this repository has audited its dividend/terminal-action evidence, else None -- audit coverage today is the 22 names in the sealed v3 survivorship audit's krTerminations list, a fact about research coverage, never an input the function reads. `window_crosses_termination` is a pure calendar fact (does this window's own exit session fall after the security's last traded session), computed the same way alpha_opportunity_v2_evaluation.target_from_sessions already decides MISSING_FORWARD_PRICE_OR_DELISTING. computedResultAsOfThisSeal.note: Computed by scripts/audit_alpha_opportunity_v4_kr_eligibility.py against the real sealed evidence -- not asserted. The NUMERIC result is unchanged from contract V1 (all 22 still excluded on both window scopes today) because the underlying per-security dividend/terminal-action evidence is exactly as incomplete as it was; what changed is that the MECHANISM computing this result no longer reads termination-list membership at all. Re-running this script against a repaired foundation would change this result without any change to the policy code or this spec.

eligibilityPolicy.correctionAppliedInThisRevision: The FIRST version of this policy (contract V1) branched on whether a security's code was in a `known_terminated_codes` set and, if so, excluded EVERY observation on it (pre- and post-termination) once its exDateSemanticsResolved read BLOCKED. That used the security's eventual termination status -- an outcome only knowable in hindsight -- as the gate deciding whether extra scrutiny applied to an observation whose own target window never touches the termination event, which is a future-survival-conditioned selection rule (a bounded, disclosed, but real instance of the same KIND of defect the US leg's NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE already named, even though the US case is structurally worse -- 0% coverage vs. a proven per-security data gap here). CONTRACT V2 removes `known_terminated_codes` and the security's own code from the eligibility FUNCTION entirely: `label_eligibility` takes only `completeness` (the sealed evidence row, or None if never audited) and `window_crosses_termination` (a pure calendar fact about the OBSERVATION's own target window, legitimate because a forward-return target is a claim about a bounded future interval by construction, exactly like the pre-existing MISSING_FORWARD_PRICE_OR_DELISTING check). Two securities with identical completeness evidence and the same window-crossing fact now receive IDENTICAL treatment regardless of whether one of them is known to terminate -- proved by tests/test_alpha_opportunity_v4.py's future-termination-invariance and future-metadata-mutation-invariance tests, which vary a synthetic terminates-later label while holding completeness fixed and assert the eligibility call does not move.
eligibilityPolicy.knownConsequence: v4's labeled sample excludes all 22 audited KR securities' observations entirely, at every signal date, under current evidence -- for a reason (a proven, per-security, zero-Yahoo-dividend-evidence data gap) that does not read termination status. This is NOT the same defect alpha-opportunity-model-v3 found in the US leg (NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE, where the panel never priced a departed name at all -- 0% coverage, structurally invisible): here the 22 names ARE priced, ARE members of the PIT KR universe on their live dates, and DO still enter feature computation and cross-sectional context -- only their own forward-return LABEL is withheld, for a disclosed, quantified, bounded and shrinking fraction of member-dates (alphaOpportunityV3SurvivorshipAudit: 3.7366% of tradable KR member-dates, 7.93% in 2013 declining to 0.76% in 2025). It is still a real, disclosed survivorship-adjacent limitation: v4's labeled sample never observes the realised forward outcome of a name whose OWN dividend evidence this repository has already found incomplete, which happens (for research-coverage reasons, not by rule) to be exactly the names that also terminate. `requiredDiagnostics.exclusionsClusterAroundTerminalEventsCheck` in evaluationPreregistration requires the future execution to publish this quantitatively rather than let it pass unremarked, and evaluationPreregistration's own verdict vocabulary must be read alongside this caveat, never as an unconditional statement about KR delisting risk.
neverAllowed: using a security's own eventual termination status, or list membership derived from it, as an input to any eligibility decision about a window that does not itself cross the termination event
treating an unresolved exchange ratio or successor as final
carrying the last traded price forward through a termination
inventing an ex-date from a record date or any other computed rule
assuming zero recovery for an unresolved termination
excluding or including an observation based on its realised return magnitude
using today's KR universe membership as a historical one
a new exclusion rule invented after an outcome is seen
eligibilityPolicy.rule: Non-crossing window (the target's own exit session is at or before the security's last traded session, or the security never terminates): ELIGIBLE if never audited (defers to production); if audited, ELIGIBLE only when exDateSemanticsResolved reads READY AND a total-return series has actually been spliced into the price panel used for labels (an engineering step this PR does not perform, so this is INELIGIBLE for every audited security today) -- never because the security is known to terminate. Crossing window (the target's own exit session is after the security's last traded session): requires terminationTypeResolved, terminalConsiderationResolved, successorResolvedWhereRequired (where the resolved type requires a successor) and terminalActionChainResolved all READY, and -- where a successor is required -- that successor's own price panel. This branch legitimately depends on the termination event because that event is INSIDE the target window being constructed.

universeWideCorroboration.interpretation: 224 of 226 (99.1%) DART-confirmed dividend-year rows across 25 outcome-blind-selected continuing names show at least one Yahoo dividend event in the same window; ZERO of the 25 show the specific all-years-zero pattern all 22 audited terminated names show. 010140.KS has no DART fiscal-year rows to check at all in this sample -- a data-absence case, category C (unknown from this evidence), neither counted as corroborating nor contradicting, and never assumed to be a genuine zero-dividend company or a vendor gap.
universeWideCorroboration.purpose: Not a full universe audit. Corroborates that treating `completeness is None` (the 213 continuing KR names never audited for dividend-basis completeness) as ELIGIBLE-by-deferral is an evidence-supported default, not a blind trust, and that the near-total Yahoo dividend blackout specific to the 22 audited terminated names is a real, distinctive, measured pattern rather than an artifact of asymmetric scrutiny alone.
universeWideCorroboration.scopeLimit: 213 of 238 continuing KR names, and all 118 REMOVED_FROM_INDEX_STILL_TRADING departed names, remain unaudited by ANY dividend-completeness check under either standard (DART ex-date confirmation or this lighter amount cross-validation). This is a disclosed, bounded research-coverage gap, never claimed to be closed by this corroboration sample, and a full-universe audit is separate, additive future data-foundation work, out of scope for this preregistration.
universeWideCorroboration.selectionMechanism: pipeline.kr_continuing_dividend_sample.select_continuing_sample: every code ranked inside the top-120 by market cap on at least one monthly snapshot, EXCLUDING the 22 terminated securities under study, ranked by how many snapshot dates it held that rank (most persistent first). Nothing about dividend completeness enters this ranking rule -- it was built to validate the DART-derivation methodology generally, before this correction ever needed it as corroborating evidence.

evaluationPreregistration.A_absoluteCalibration: date-balanced pooled realised = a + b * predicted net relative return (not within-date demeaned); b lower > 0; a and b intervals published; MSE improvement over training mean lower > 0
evaluationPreregistration.B_ordering: equal-date rank IC lower > 0; within-date slope lower > 0
evaluationPreregistration.C_probability: Brier and log-loss improvement over training prevalence (net label) lower > 0; pooled date-balanced ECE upper <= 0.05 (v2 simulated null recorded in v2 spec)
evaluationPreregistration.D_disclosedBesideNotGating: D recomputed separately for EXPECTATION_POSITIVE_OUTPERFORM_PROBABILITY_NOT_ABOVE_HALF and FITTED_INTERVAL_SPANS_OUTSIDE_OPTION subsets, descriptive only
evaluationPreregistration.D_positiveExpectedAlphaRegion: on dates with >= 1 POSITIVE_EXPECTED_ALPHA name: date-mean realised net relative return of those names lower > 0 (the outside-option test) AND same-date spread over non-positive names lower > 0 (lesser of level and spread); plus, disclosed not gated, realised-on-predicted slope inside the positive region and realised means by within-date terciles of predicted expectedNetAlpha among positive names (terciles fixed from predictions alone); no predicted-alpha threshold other than 0 is ever evaluated
evaluationPreregistration.E_stability: annual folds >= 70% jointly positive (rank IC, Brier, MSE); D point estimate positive in each chronological half; no subgroup beyond the two horizons
evaluationPreregistration.F_missingnessIntegrity: before ANY gate in A-E may be interpreted, the execution report MUST publish every field in `requiredDiagnostics` below; a report missing one is not a partial result, it is DATA_INSUFFICIENT for every claim
evaluationPreregistration.dependence: moving blocks of 26 whole weekly dates, 2000 draws, seed 42, Bonferroni across the two horizon claims (21D, 126D): twoSidedTail=0.0125, 97.5% two-sided intervals
evaluationPreregistration.status: PREREGISTERED_BEFORE_ANY_OUTCOME; not executable in this PR

executionDataVersioning.rationale: Separates three different promises that a single byte-pin conflated in the first sealed version: what the POLICY guarantees (immutable), what the FOUNDATION is allowed to do (improve monotonically, checked), and what one EXECUTION RUN actually used (frozen once, checked again if read twice, never outcome-selected).

tiers.executionSnapshot: whichever current foundation state a specific execution run reads MUST be frozen -- hashed via pipeline.alpha_opportunity_v4_eligibility.freeze_execution_snapshot and recorded immutably in that run's own output report -- exactly once, BEFORE the run constructs its first label. The run must call assert_snapshot_matches_frozen_hash before any later step that reads the foundation again, and must never select among candidate snapshots, or re-read a newer one mid-run, based on which produces a more favourable result. Once outcome computation starts, the execution dataset/version does not change.
tiers.foundation: the KR terminal-action reconstruction artifacts may improve monotonically before an execution starts -- pipeline.alpha_opportunity_v4_eligibility.assert_foundation_not_regressed proves a later snapshot only ever adds READY fields relative to the snapshot cited in sourceFoundationCitation, never removes one.
tiers.policy: sealed by this preregistration; pipeline/alpha_opportunity_v4_eligibility.py's decision logic and reason codes are frozen and verified by dependencyHashes on every load.

formerV3BlockersResolvedByPolicy.resolution: v3 treated this as a design blocker because it had no predeclared treatment. v4 predeclares one: label_eligibility excludes every observation for which this repository has audited and found an unresolved dividend-basis gap, by a computed, machine-checked rule that reads only the security's own evidence -- never its termination status. The underlying dividend/ex-date data itself is unchanged and unrepaired.

Same mechanism: a window crossing termination is INELIGIBLE under the policy above unless the full terminal-action chain is READY, which is true for 0 of 22 today. No unresolved consideration is ever used.

governingDocumentConflict.whatTheyStated: Both documents' own 'exact next step' / final determination sections state a v4 preregistration should be drafted only once every applicable completeness-matrix field reads READY ('never before, and never by loosening this matrix's own rules'), and that the operator action remaining was a workflow retry, not a v4 draft.
governingDocumentConflict.whyV4IsCreatedAnyway: The retry named as the remaining operator action has now been run (GitHub Actions run 36264244053, 2026-09-26) and confirmed exhausted: all 38 previously-failed DART receipts failed again with the same retained error, and every other evidence-recovery route (direct HTTPS, WebFetch, workflow_dispatch with a real token) was already confirmed exhausted by PR #158 itself. There is no further repair action available in this environment. This PR's own governing task explicitly requires a v4 preregistration now, built on a NEW study-level eligibility-policy concept that predeclares treatment of the remaining gap rather than waiting on a repair this environment cannot perform -- see docs/alpha-opportunity-model-v4-preregistration.md's own framing. This is a real conflict between the prior documents' stated gate and this PR's instructions, resolved here by: (a) never editing `docs/results/kr-terminal-action-reconstruction-v2.json`'s `foundationStatus` away from PARTIALLY_REPAIRED, (b) introducing the SOURCE FOUNDATION / STUDY DESIGN / EXECUTION three-layer distinction the prior documents did not contemplate, and (c) an eligibility policy that excludes rather than repairs the affected observations, so no completeness-matrix field is loosened and no value is invented to force a READY reading of the matrix itself.

newInteractions.rationale: Section 11 of this study's own governing task requires any interaction to be selected on economic mechanism, PIT availability, adequate historical coverage and manageable multiplicity -- never on outcome data. Every candidate hypothesis that needs investor flow (candidate 5, flow confirmation x price/attention) is excluded above as access-unproven. The remaining candidates (fundamental state/change x liquidity shock; price leadership x liquidity persistence; weak fundamentals x liquidity shock; attention x price-leadership divergence) all involve the same small, already-carried-forward KR feature set (relative126, acceleration21, vol63, logVolumeShock60, shockPersistence5d, volumePriceAlignment, and three DART accounting fields dark before 2015) that v1-v3 never found PIT-unsafe but also never tested in combination. Rather than add an untested interaction term to a preregistration whose purpose is closing a DATA-INTEGRITY gap, v4 carries v3's linear/shallow-HGB-complement model family unchanged, which already lets the shallow HGB complement (never a decision, per carriedFromV3.models.interpretation) surface any such interaction as complementary evidence without this spec committing to one by name. A dedicated interaction study, if warranted, is a separate preregistration.

scope.conservativeBaseline: a conservative baseline model over v3's already-vetted KR feature set and model family; not a test of any new interaction (see newInteractions) and not a re-tune of alpha-reliability-v1's closed calibration or alpha-risk-separation-v1's closed sleeve questions; its failure or blockage says nothing about those
scope.regions: KR-only. US carries a separate, structurally different survivorship defect (NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE: the panel never priced 212 of 324 departed S&P 500 identities at all, so termination is invisible, not merely basis-inconsistent) that this PR does not touch, repair, or wait for. Region symmetry is not a reason to hold KR back: alpha-research-philosophy-v2 section 1 already states 'treating US and KR as one model, or as two models forever' is not required, and regional-alpha-research-separation-v1 already separated the two before this PR existed.
